Package org.apache.juneau.rest.server.filter

Record Class HandshakeHosts

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
org.apache.juneau.rest.server.filter.HandshakeHosts
Record Components:
values - The Host values, in order. Empty when there is no Host and no authority to stand in for it. Never null.
synthesised - true if values is the single value built from the request URI rather than a real Host header.
public record HandshakeHosts(List<String> values, boolean synthesised) extends Record
The Host values of a WebSocket handshake; over RFC 8441 with no Host, one value from the request URI's authority.

A handshake over HTTP/2 (RFC 8441 extended CONNECT) carries its authority as the :authority pseudo-header and no Host header, which a servlet container surfaces in the handshake's request URI. A JSR 356 HandshakeRequest exposes no protocol, so the HTTP/2 case is recognized by what an RFC 6455 handshake must carry and an RFC 8441 one does not: a Sec-WebSocket-Key or Upgrade header. The container enforces that signal on Jetty and Tomcat (a key-less HTTP/1.1 upgrade is a 400 before any configurator runs).

Header names are matched ignoring case, because HTTP/2 field names arrive in lower case.

Since:
10.0.0

  • Method Details

    • of

      public static HandshakeHosts of(Map<String,List<String>> headers, URI requestUri)
      The Host values of a handshake.
      1. Every real Host value, across all spellings of the name, is returned as is.
      2. Otherwise, if the handshake has a Sec-WebSocket-Key or Upgrade header (any value, blank included), it is an RFC 6455 handshake and the result is empty.
      3. Otherwise one value is built from the request URI: its host (IPv6 brackets kept) plus ":" and its port when one is given. No port is invented, so the caller's scheme default applies. Userinfo is never carried. A null URI, or one with no host, gives the empty result.
      Parameters:
      headers - The handshake headers. Can be null, which is empty.
      requestUri - The handshake's request URI. Can be null.
      Returns:
      The hosts. Never null.
